estate-table

One look and one behaviour for plain HTML tables — a stylesheet and a small script. Sort, filter, format, page, and copy to a spreadsheet or an email. No framework, no build step, nothing generated: you write a normal <table>, add class names, and link two files. With JavaScript off, the reader still gets the whole table.

See it working

Every class and every behaviour, on invented figures. Click a header to sort (dates, money and text each by their own rules, within each band), type in the boxes to filter, and use the green button to copy into a spreadsheet or an email.

The example as a page of your own

The whole page above, from <!doctype html> to </html>. Save it as a .html file and open it: it needs only the two files on the CDN.

<!doctype html>

<head>

  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Estate table — every feature</title>

  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@ploutosservices/estate-table@1/table/estate-table.js" defer></script>
</head>
<body style="font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 1rem; color: rgb(17 24 39);">

Use it

<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@ploutosservices/estate-table@1/table/estate-table.css">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@ploutosservices/estate-table@1/table/estate-table.js" defer></script>

(or https://unpkg.com/@ploutosservices/estate-table@1/table/…, or npm install @ploutosservices/estate-table). @1 follows every 1.x release; pin an exact version (@1.0.0) to freeze it. The icons the stylesheet draws are loaded from ../icons/ beside it, so keep the package's folders together if you host the files yourself.

The whole contract is SPEC.md: every class and attribute, what each does, and which renderer has measured it. Questions and issues: https://github.com/ploutosservices/estate-table/issues

Under React

The plain script works under React as it is. Where React owns the rows, table/estate-table-react.js is a second renderer of the same markup — one ES module, no JSX, no build; react and react-dom are your page's imports:

import { Estate } from '@ploutosservices/estate-table/table/estate-table-react.js';
// <Estate>{ the same markup: a box with its band, scroller and footer, or a plain table }</Estate>

Estate takes no prop but its children. Every row and cell must be an element in the tree you give it — a component may draw what is inside a cell, never a row or a cell itself. SPEC.md marks what it has not built (estate-copy-box draws each table's own copy pair instead).

The skeleton

<div class="estate-table-box">
  <div class="estate-table-title">Payments</div>
  <div class="estate-table-scroll">
    <table class="estate-table estate-sort estate-filter estate-copy">
      <thead><tr><th>Date</th><th>Payee</th><th class="estate-num">Amount</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>2026-10-01</td><td>ACME</td><td class="estate-num">1,250.00</td></tr>
        <tr class="estate-total"><td>Total</td><td></td><td class="estate-num">1,250.00</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
  <div class="estate-table-footer">1 row</div>
</div>

The look — classes

classonwhat it does
estate-table-box · estate-table-title · estate-table-actions · estate-table-toolbar · estate-table-scroll · estate-table-footer · estate-table-notethe wrapper and its partsframed box, title band with buttons at its right, a strip for your own controls, a wide table scrolling inside, a footer band; a plain line under a table outside any box
estate-tabletablethe table itself
estate-numtd and its thright-aligned, tabular figures
estate-text · estate-sm · estate-mono · estate-center · estate-nowrapcellsbody size · small · monospace · centred · never wraps
estate-action · estate-link · estate-labelcellsnarrow icon column · hand cursor and hover tint · label column of a label/value table
estate-total · estate-row-sectiontrtotals row · group band
estate-fit · estate-numbered · estate-striped · estate-toptable (estate-fit on the box too)content width · a row-number column · visible stripes · top-aligned cells
estate-stickythe boxthe header row stays in view while the table scrolls inside the box; data-rows="8" or data-height="calc(100vh - 12rem)" on the box says how tall
estate-narrow · estate-mediumthe boxat most 32rem · 42rem wide
estate-pina column's th and tdsthe column stays in view while a wide table scrolls sideways (the script places a second pinned column after the first)
estate-link holding one <a>tdthe link fills the cell
estate-tint-primary … -darktable, tr, td, theight hand-picked tints

Every colour, size and space is a CSS variable (--estate-table-*) at the top of the stylesheet — override them on :root to restyle.

The behaviour — opt in by class

class / attributeonwhat happens
estate-sorttableclick a header (or Enter): ascending, descending, back to the opening order; shift-click adds a column after the ones in force
data-sort-by="3 desc, 1"tablethe order the table opens in (columns from 1)
estate-filtertableone box above the table — every word typed must appear in the row; "N of M shown"
estate-filter-columnstablea row of boxes under the headers, one per column, all applied together: text matches any part of the value (the column's values are offered as you type); a number column also takes >1000, <=50, =50, 1000..5000; a filtering column's header is marked; a button in the bar, or f while you are in the table, shows or hides the row
estate-drop-emptytablehides every column whose data cells are all empty (totals and group bands do not count; an icon does); re-judged after every filter, so a column comes back when a row that fills it does
estate-text-filterththis column's box is always text, even when every value is a number
estate-as-text · estate-idththe column is text for every rule · holds identities (by size when all digits, never formatted, every digit kept in a copy)
estate-keepththe column stays under estate-drop-empty even when empty
data-filter-row="hidden"tablethe column boxes open hidden until the reader chooses
estate-formatth or tablenumbers formatted: grouped thousands, data-decimals on the th or table, else the most any value shows; the copy carries the value as it arrived
estate-sumtd in a tr.estate-totalthe script writes the column's sum over the rows the filters leave
estate-pagetablea pager in the footer: data-page-size, data-page-sizes="5 10 20", the reader's choice remembered under data-store="key"
data-total="631"tablethe rows are part of a larger set on the server; the count says so
data-href="…"td.estate-linkthe cell opens the address: a click, a Ctrl- or middle click (new tab), Enter
data-source="#id"tablethe copy and the export read that other (hidden, fuller) table
estate-exceltablean Excel button beside the copy button when a workbook writer is on the page (a global ExcelJS); inert without one. data-excel-href="…" and data-excel-title="…" make it a link to your own workbook instead
data-peek="…"any element in the tablehovering or focusing it shows a card holding what the address answers (fetched once, as the page itself would)
estate-resizetabledrag a header's right edge to make the column wider or narrower; remembered under data-store
estate-copytablea copy button (title band, else caption, else a bar above the table): text/html with inline styles for Excel, Google Sheets and Gmail, plus tab-separated text/plain
estate-no-sortththis column is not sortable
estate-sort-absth or tablenumbers sort by size, sign ignored
estate-copy-bodytablethe copy leaves the tfoot out
estate-copy-markuptablea second button copying the table's HTML as text — structure and cell text only, for a page's source
estate-keep-foottablethe tfoot rows stay shown while a filter narrows the rows
estate-copy-box.estate-table-boxone copy pair on the box's band copies every table in the box, in order; no table in it draws its own
data-sort="…"tdsort the cell by this value instead of its text
data-raw="…"tdthe plain-text copy carries this value instead of the formatted text
  • A column has one type, or it is text: dates (ISO — a timestamp with a zone such as Z or -04:00 is compared in UTC — 11 May 2011, May 11, 2011 — never 05/11/2011, which means two different days), phone numbers ((305) 555-1212, 305.555.1212, +1 305 555 1212 — compared as digit strings), numbers ($1,234.50, -1,234.50, (1,234.50), 12%), else text — case- and accent-insensitive, Item 9 before Item 10. Empty cells sort last both ways.
  • Groups and totals stay in place: rows sort within each group band — a tr.estate-row-section, or any row that is one cell spanning the table — and an estate-total row stays after the rows it sums. While a filter narrows the rows, totals (in the body or the tfoot) are hidden: they no longer sum what is shown — unless the script sums them (estate-sum), which is true again.
  • A copy is what is shown: current order, filtered-out rows and hidden columns left out, numbers unformatted in the plain text (as text: a long id keeps every digit).
  • A table added after load: document.dispatchEvent(new Event('estate:tables-added')), or EstateTable.init(root). data-manual on the script element stops it decorating anything on load, so your announcement, or EstateTable.init/.refresh, is the only start.
  • A cell may hold a form control: a select is what it shows, a checkbox ✓ or nothing, a field its value. A header that shows only an icon is labelled by its aria-label. EstateTable.tooltip = (node, text) => … draws the script's tooltips your way.
  • Rows that change after load need nothing: each table watches its own body, so rows a framework re-renders or a reload replaces get the current sort, filters and empty-column hiding, and a table drawn empty gets its controls when its rows arrive. To say it yourself: dispatch estate:rows-changed on the table, or call EstateTable.refresh(root).
